name: v0.3.21 return-waypoint frontier escape
research_question: After a handoff-resolved outer sequence resumes returning, does abandoning the return obligation at a previously visited intermediate hub that still has residual local or structural frontier repair the shared v0.3.20 template 5/8/9 loss without a successful-return fabrication and without losing the frozen composite or historical gates?
hypothesis: After handoff resolution, the composite candidate keeps the outer list-to-entity sequence alive as a return obligation. When that return path re-enters the known entity hub, it continues to the original list parent and starves already-observed residual frontier on the entity waypoint.
not: permission to change the product default
permission to retune after the candidate freeze
a claim that the mechanism recovers every bug before the experiment
causal_language_allowed: entity local actions were observable but skipped
open_side was residual at the first waypoint and either absent or delayed
causal_language_forbidden: this proves the mechanism will recover every bug

mechanism.name: Return-Waypoint Frontier Escape
mechanism.required_provenance: parent_frame_resume_to_return for the same active sequence, from the existing handoff lifecycle
true_return_required: ledger.returning is true before the step
action is an existing return action
intermediate_waypoint: active resumed outer sequence still exists
destination state exists and is usable
destination cluster is not the original final parent cluster
destination cluster was visited earlier in the same active outer sequence during outbound exploration
no crash or unwind cleared the obligation
mechanism.visited_hubs: candidate-local, browser-observed states only, cluster-aware, exact variants share a cluster, reset clears them, historical frames are not mutated
mechanism.residual_frontier: at least one residual local button using the v0.3.17 eligible-button rule, or one residual structural branch using the frozen structural branch classification
mechanism.residual_source: current GUIState, current visible actions, BranchLedger, structural memory, and local-action drained keys
excluded_from_residual: generic nav-up or back action classified as return
mechanism.escape: emit return_waypoint_frontier_escape, abandon the return obligation, do not select a frontier action, clear returning and commitment, preserve the physical waypoint, then let the frozen normal policy choose the next action
mechanism.terminal_rationale: Historical LEGAL_TERMINALS cannot be edited. The legal abandoned outcome is paired with the specific audit event. Exactly one terminal is emitted. return_success is not incremented and returned is not emitted.
mechanism.suppression_rationale: Cluster alone is too broad across sequences. Sequence-instance alone is too narrow for an equivalent recreated branch. Branch key plus waypoint cluster is the stable key. A new branch key may escape at the same cluster. Reset clears keys.
precedence: final parent completion wins over waypoint escape
early parent re-entry completion wins over waypoint escape
exact-repeat return-cycle escape on the same step wins and blocks a second escape
unresolved child or handoff stack depth greater than 0 blocks waypoint escape
crash or unusable destination blocks waypoint escape

gates.outcome_A_guard_recovery: confirmed(Guard) subset_of confirmed(v0.3.21) on all four v0.3.20 positives

scope: inspected repair of the v0.3.20 fresh targets, not fresh validation
